title: DySpMM: From Fix to Dynamic for Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication Accelerators
problem: FPGA-based SpMM accelerators with fixed configurations suffer from three key limitations: suboptimal sub-matrix partitioning that increases memory access for dynamic sparsity patterns, fixed row-wise allocation causing workload imbalance, and read-after-write hazards from floating-point adders that require time-consuming pre-processing.
motivation: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication is a critical operator across many domains with inherently dynamic sparsity, element distribution, and data dependency patterns that fixed architectures cannot efficiently accommodate.
method: DySpMM introduces dynamic design methodology through three components: a configurable data distributor that adapts sub-matrix size to sparsity patterns, an element-wise allocator for dynamic load balancing across processing elements, and an interleaved reorder unit that resolves RAW hazards at runtime without pre-processing. The architecture is implemented on Xilinx U280 FPGA with configurable dataflow that adjusts to input characteristics.
key_novelty: Dynamic reconfiguration of SpMM accelerator dataflow and element allocation at runtime to adapt to variable sparsity, distribution, and data dependencies rather than relying on fixed configurations.
contributions: Configurable data distributor enabling dynamic sub-matrix sizing for adaptive memory access optimization (up to 3.79× reduction)
Element-wise allocator achieving dynamic workload balancing across processing elements (up to 3.74× utilization improvement)
Interleaved reorder unit eliminating RAW hazards at runtime without expensive pre-processing
FPGA implementation demonstrating 1.42× throughput gain over Sextans and 1.78× energy efficiency over V100S GPU
primary_theme: dynamic sparse matrix multiplication acceleration on FPGA
